Observed command `TMPDIR=/tmp CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo test -p cadence --lib --bin cadence gap15`: all seven gap151 tests passed within 20 library and 23 binary passes, zero failures. The separately reported resolved-policy race is a new goal-backward gap, not the original absence of any admission path.

truths.truth: The execution handoff carries one resolved gate and routing answer into the admission it exposes
truths.evidence: behavior wrong - crates/cadence/src/execution_service.rs:2330-2345 resolves the execution boundary's route and diff gate, and execution_review_decision retains that gate, but :2362-2365 builds a request containing neither the resolved gate nor routing evidence; :2371 discards the returned gate with `..` and :2372 calls review_service::admit. That function refreshes configuration and routing again at crates/cadence/src/review_service.rs:206-226 and derives a second gate at :244-286. Concrete failing scenario: a completed receipt d1 has no saved review binding; the outer read resolves diff=advisory, then a concurrent config apply changes diff=off before admit's refresh. The second read returns no-review, crates/cadence/src/execution_service.rs:2377 treats that as skip, and execute-next/apply can expose continuation with no fire, manifest, or attempt even though the boundary's applicable resolved policy required review. The inverse ordering also shows the eager seam: :2346 calls risk_material before the off decision at :2366, so an off gate can fail on review-only material instead of cleanly skipping. The observed gap151 tests all pass because they test execution_review_decision with an already-built request and test the handler with stubbed answers; none carries the production-resolved gate/routing through the real admit call.
